text:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH - log rate spike detected for service=redwood-inference (model-inference-prod). Alert: log_rate.rules/500s-spike. Count: 380 errors in last 5m. Pager: @oncall (jordan)

maya: saw this — dashboards show a big jump in 5xxs ~10:02. impact: increased p50 latency for gen endpoints but most are 502/503.

sam: any customer-facing errors reported? support.csv shows a couple of tickets but nothing widespread yet.

jordan: I'm on it. pulling logs now. suspecting quota bursts hitting a backend cache and returning 502.

ryan: if it's cache, we can flip to fallback pool, but need confirmation. what's the log query that fired?

jordan: the alert uses this log query:```logql
service=redwood-inference level=error status_code>=500 | count_over_time(5m)
```

maya: digging into a subset with model and backend tags:```logql
service=redwood-inference level=error status_code=502 model=\"gpt-small\" backend=kv-cache | unwrap message | limit 100
```

jordan: results: lots of "cache miss: connection reset" + backend io timeouts. sample line: `cache-client.go:142 timeout writing to connection`

ops-bot: automated mitigation suggestion: suppress noisy alert for 15m if an operator acknowledges. :gear:

sam: we should avoid suppressing globally. propose: tighten alert with regex to ignore known transient KV connect failures during deployment windows, or lower cardinality by grouping.

maya: agree. quick live mitigation: add a temporary suppression on the pager rule and create a targeted rule that excludes `cache-client.go:142` signature so we don't drown other signals.

jordan: acknowledged suppression for 10m (manual). I'll also add a fallback routing to the replica pool for the affected backend to reduce failed requests.

ryan: if you need me I can flip the pool routing — but prefer we make it an automated fallback in the router.

sre-liz: logging a TODO: post-incident, update the log-based rule to include a negative regex for the known non-actionable line, and add a dashboard panel for KV backend error rate.

maya: here's a suggested updated query to reduce noise:```logql
service=redwood-inference level=error status_code>=500 | regexp_replace("cache-client.go:142.*", "") | count_over_time(5m)
```but better is to add an explicit filter:```logql
service=redwood-inference level=error status_code>=500 AND message !~ "cache-client.go:142" | count_over_time(5m)
```

sam: also add a grouped alert to fire only if unique(service, backend) > 1 to avoid single-host flaps.

jordan: live update: flipped routing to fallback pool at 10:12 — error rate started to decline. p50 latency back to normal for most routes.

ops-bot: note: created incident channel #inc-1816007890 and attached trace links.

maya: customer impact assessment: small subset of requests saw 502s for ~8 minutes. Roughly 0.2% of total traffic. Raised 3 customer tickets. No major SLA breaches detected.

ryan: passing to infra to follow up on KV connection stability. Suggestion: increase client-side retry window and add circuit breaker to avoid saturating backend.

sre-liz: Post-incident actions (quick list):
- PR to update log rule: add `message !~ \"cache-client.go:142\"`
- Add a new saved dashboard panel for kv-backend 5xx rate
- Add a regression test / synthetic to catch KV saturation
- Consider grouping alert by backend and add capacity-based thresholding

maya: I'll own the PR for the log rule and dashboard. ETA EOD. Jordan, can you add the runbook step about fallback pool?

jordan: yes added step in runbook and assigned follow-ups to ryan for infra root cause.

sam: can we also add an eval to Optimize that looks at token burst patterns? might have been traffic spike from one customer.

maya: noted. will sync with product on traffic patterns tomorrow.

jordan: handing off to next on-call (ryan) at 10:30. leaving suppression for another 10m to avoid noise while we stabilize.

ryan: taking over. thanks team. I'll triage infra tasks and file the postmortem draft after we validate logs.

incident-bot: Incident closed (stabilized) at 10:35 — summary: transient KV connection failures caused a brief spike in 502s, mitigated by switching to fallback pool and suppressing noisy alert. Follow-ups assigned. :white_check_mark:
